name: urinary tract obstruction overview
title: Urinary tract obstruction decision chart: an upper-tract block from a stone (renal colic) sorted by fever and stone size into an infected obstructing stone needing urgent drainage, a small stone likely to pass, or a large or failing stone needing lithotripsy or nephrolithotomy; a lower-tract block (urinary retention at the bladder outlet) relieved by catheter with watch for post-obstructive diuresis; plus how to prevent the next stone

root.title: Urine flow BLOCKED: WHERE, and how BAD?
lines: hydronephrosis (dilated pelvis + calyces) on ultrasound or computed tomography (CT) · it can occur WITHOUT a block (reflux)
worse if: COMPLETE · BOTH sides · INFECTED (speeds nephron loss) · > 6 WEEKS complete = function lost for good

groups.title: UPPER tract, one side: RENAL COLIC from a stone
lines: severe one-sided flank pain in WAVES → groin, scrotum or labia · hematuria · vomiting
1 · CT (most sensitive) · ultrasound sees every stone · plain x-ray MISSES uric acid stones
~also think: aortic aneurysm, pyelonephritis, a mass, musculoskeletal

head: h
Obstructing stone + FEVER
SURGICAL EMERGENCY
clue: • antibiotics can't work until it drains

head: h
Stone likely to PASS
tx: anti-inflammatory (ketorolac) or a short opioid course
relaxes the ureter: medical expulsive therapy

head: h
Stone to REMOVE
clue: • renal failure: solitary kidney, poor function
tx: • in the URETER: ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy

head: h
Urinary retention
can't void
clue: urine can't be concentrated → K ↑, metabolic acidosis
tx: • Na + water lost after BOTH sides are relieved
